section: Governor - appointment, powers, discretionary powers, position and controversies (Article 200/201, Article 356 reports)
subsections: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)

accepted.s: Under Article 153 of the Constitution, which of the following is permissible?
o: A single Governor may be appointed for two or more States
A State may function without a Governor for an indefinite period
Only Union Territories can have a common Governor
A Governor may be elected jointly by two State Legislatures
accepted.x: Article 153 provides for a Governor for each State, while the Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 enables one person to serve as Governor of two or more States.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional exception to the general rule instead of choosing the broad statement.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The appointment of a Governor under Article 155 is made through which of the following instruments?
o: Order issued by the Chief Justice of India
Warrant under the hand and seal of the President
Resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha
Notification issued by the Union Cabinet
accepted.x: Article 155 provides that the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
accepted.tq: Use the exact constitutional expression to distinguish the appointing authority from the appointing instrument.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the office of Governor:
1. The Governor is directly elected by the people of the State.
2. The Governor is indirectly elected by the elected members of the State Legislature.
3. The Governor is appointed by the President.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
3 only
1 and 2 only
accepted.x: The Governor is appointed by the President and is neither directly nor indirectly elected.
accepted.tq: Reject both forms of election and identify the constitutionally prescribed method of appointment.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the constitutional position regarding the tenure of a Governor?
o: The Governor holds office for six years unless removed by the State Legislature.
The Governor holds office for five years and may continue until the successor enters office.
The Governor necessarily vacates office on completion of five years, even if no successor has entered office.
The Governor has a fixed tenure which cannot be interrupted by transfer.
accepted.x: The normal term is five years, but the Governor continues in office until the successor enters office. The Governor may also be transferred before completion of the term.
accepted.tq: Focus on the distinction between the normal term and automatic cessation of office.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Governor may resign by addressing the resignation to the President.
2. A Governor may be transferred by the President.
3. A Governor may be reappointed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: A Governor resigns to the President, may be transferred, and may be reappointed. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Combine three related tenure provisions and select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a qualification prescribed under Article 157 for appointment as Governor?
o: Residence in the State concerned for at least five years
Being a citizen at the time of appointment
Completion of 35 years of age
Citizenship of India
accepted.x: Article 157 requires the person to be a citizen of India and to have completed 35 years of age. Residence in the concerned State is not a constitutional qualification.
accepted.tq: Find the additional-looking condition that is not part of the constitutional qualification.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Article 158, consider the following statements:
1. A Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or of a State Legislature.
2. A Governor cannot hold any other office of profit.
3. The emoluments of a Governor are fixed by the concerned State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: A Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature and cannot hold an office of profit. The emoluments are fixed by Parliament by law, not by the State Legislature.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong authority trap in the statement concerning fixation of emoluments.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Article)

accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: If the Chief Justice of a State High Court is unavailable to administer the Governor's oath, who ordinarily administers it?
o: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
The senior-most judge of that High Court
The Chief Minister of the State
The President of India
accepted.x: In the absence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, the oath is administered by the senior-most judge of that High Court.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional fallback arrangement to an absence scenario.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the emoluments of a Governor is correct?
o: They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
They are determined annually by the State Cabinet.
They are paid from the Contingency Fund of the State.
They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India in every case.
accepted.x: The emoluments of a Governor are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State under Article 202(3). They cannot be reduced during the Governor's term, and Parliament fixes them by law.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the charged expenditure of the State from other constitutional funds.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When one person is appointed Governor of two or more States, the expenditure relating to the Governor's emoluments is shared in the manner determined by the
o: Union Finance Commission
Inter-State Council
President
Governors' Conference
accepted.x: Where one Governor serves two or more States, the President determines the allocation of the cost of emoluments among those States.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority settles the financial consequence of a common constitutional office.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following represents the convention generally followed in appointing a Governor?
1. The Governor is ordinarily selected from outside the State.
2. The Chief Minister of the State is consulted.
3. The Constitution expressly requires that the Governor must be an outsider.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: By convention, the Governor is generally an outsider and the State Chief Minister is consulted. The Constitution does not expressly mandate that the Governor must be an outsider.
accepted.tq: Separate constitutional requirements from conventions by rejecting the absolute wording in statement 3.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the pleasure doctrine applicable to a Governor:
1. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
2. The pleasure of the President permits removal of a Governor for any arbitrary reason without constitutional limitation.
3. The grounds for removal of a Governor are expressly enumerated in the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
accepted.x: Article 156 incorporates the President's pleasure, but B.P. Singhal v. Union of India held that the power cannot be exercised arbitrarily. The Constitution does not expressly enumerate grounds for removal.
accepted.tq: Treat an apparently broad power as subject to constitutional limits and judicial review.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court's decision in B.P. Singhal v. Union of India (2010) established that
o: the Governor's office is completely independent of the President's pleasure
a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or merely because the Centre's Government has changed
a Governor can be removed only after impeachment by Parliament
a Governor can be removed whenever the Union Government changes
accepted.x: The pleasure doctrine is not unfettered: removal cannot be arbitrary or based merely on a change in the Government at the Centre. Such removal is open to limited judicial review.
accepted.tq: Use the case-law principle to reject both absolute executive power and the invented impeachment procedure.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): A Governor cannot be removed merely because the Government at the Centre has changed.
Reason (R): The President's pleasure under Article 156 is subject to constitutional limitations and cannot be exercised arbitrarily.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. The limitation on arbitrary exercise of the President's pleasure explains why a change of the Central Government alone cannot justify removal.
accepted.tq: Check whether the legal principle stated in the Reason directly explains the protection stated in the Assertion.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: To which of the following bodies is the Governor constitutionally answerable in the ordinary discharge of the office?
o: The State Legislative Assembly alone
The Council of Ministers of the State alone
The Lok Sabha alone
None of the above
accepted.x: The Governor is not answerable to either House of Parliament, to the State Legislature, or to the State Council of Ministers.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-accountability trap and select the option covering all three excluded bodies.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 200, reservation of a State Bill for the consideration of the President is mandatory when the Bill
o: concerns any matter relating to State taxation
endangers the constitutional position of the High Court
relates to the appointment of the State Public Service Commission
has been passed without the recommendation of the Chief Minister
accepted.x: Reservation is mandatory for a Bill that, in the Governor's opinion, endangers the position of the High Court. This power is regarded as an instrument of central control over the States.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific constitutional trigger instead of treating every important State Bill as reservable.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What is the effect of the President's decision on a Bill reserved by the Governor under Article 200?
o: The Supreme Court automatically becomes the final legislative authority.
The President has an absolute veto over the reserved Bill.
The State Legislature may enact the Bill despite the President's rejection.
The Governor may enact the Bill without further action.
accepted.x: A Bill reserved for the President's consideration is subject to the President's absolute veto. The State Legislature cannot override that rejection by itself.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the President's final power over a reserved Bill from the ordinary legislative process.
accepted.sec: Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)  [APPSC]
